scenes.title: Covering Index
scenes.narration: A covering index holds every column a query needs, so the query can be answered from the index without touching the table.

scenes.title: Why it is fast
bullets: It contains all columns the query filters and returns
The engine reads the index alone — an index-only scan
The expensive key lookup into the table disappears
scenes.narration: A covering index contains every column the query filters on and every column it returns. Because the whole answer lives in the index, the engine performs an index-only scan. The per-row key lookup into the base table simply disappears, which is what makes covering indexes so fast.

scenes.title: Cover the query with INCLUDE
scenes.code:
-- Key columns are searchable; INCLUDE columns ride along
CREATE INDEX ix_orders_cust_cover
    ON orders (customer_id)
    INCLUDE (order_date, total);

-- Fully covered: no lookup to the table
SELECT order_date, total
FROM orders
WHERE customer_id = 42;
scenes.narration: Here customer_id is the searchable key, while order_date and total ride along in the INCLUDE clause. When the query filters by customer_id and returns those two columns, everything it needs is already in the index. The engine answers it entirely from the index with no lookup back to the table.

scenes.title: With and without covering

left.title: Non-covering index
points: Extra random I/O per matched row

scenes.narration: With a non-covering index the engine seeks the keys and then does a key lookup for each row to fetch the missing columns, adding random I/O. With a covering index the seek finds the keys and every needed column is already there, so the query completes as an index-only scan with zero lookups.

scenes.text: Covering indexes speed reads but widen the index and cost more to maintain on writes. Cover your hottest queries, not every query.
scenes.narration: Covering indexes dramatically speed reads, but the extra columns widen the index and add maintenance cost on every write. Reserve them for your hottest queries rather than applying them everywhere.

scenes.text: Put filter columns in the key and returned columns in INCLUDE, and the query is served entirely from the index — the fastest read path there is.
scenes.narration: Place the filter columns in the key and the returned columns in INCLUDE, and the query is served entirely from the index, which is the fastest read path a database can offer.
